jobs.occupation: Doctoral Research Fellowship in Multi-Omics at Centre for Precision Psychiatry
jobs.description:
About the position
We have an available position as a doctoral research fellow (SKO 1017) at the University of Oslo, 3-years engagement, affiliated with the Centre for Precision Psychiatry, Institute of Clinical Medicine, University of Oslo and the Department of Medical Genetics, Oslo University Hospital.
 
The Centre runs a series of multidisciplinary studies involving hospital departments and several research groups at the University of Oslo, building on advanced statistical methods for analysis of large-scale human genetic, proteomic, metabolomic, and neuroimaging data. The Centre has access to large databases of biomarkers, clinical and cognitive variables, genotyping and sequencing data, and MRI brain imaging data. In addition, we actively collaborate with large international consortia, particularly the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC), ENIGMA, and the European Alzheimer’s Disease DNA BioBank (EADB) and have access to data from Norwegian population cohorts (e.g., DemGene, HUNT, HUSK, the Tromsø Study, MoBa), as well as the UK Biobank, Estonian Biobank and ADNI. 

For more information, please visit: https://www.ous-research.no/djurovic/
Project description
The available position is part of the Back2Future project, entitled Multimodal metabolic markers for mechanisms and predictive trajectories of Alzheimer’s disease, funded by the Research Council of Norway's TOPPFORSK programme and led by Professor Srdjan Djurovic. The project aims to identify heritable, early metabolic and protein biomarkers in blood that can predict the risk of Alzheimer's disease decades before symptoms appear, by combining metabolomics and proteomics with genetics, brain MRI, cognition and health registry data from large Norwegian and Nordic cohorts.

To achieve this goal, the researcher hired for this doctoral research fellowship position will work with the project's datasets, analytical methodology, and computational tools, including state-of-the-art data storage and research infrastructure hosted at the Services for Sensitive Data (TSD).

The PhD fellow will work with large-scale analytical tools to integrate multi-omics with brain imaging data to identify early biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease risk and contribute to development of a personalized prediction algorithm.

The duration of appointment is 3 years and is available from January 2027, with possibility of a flexible start date.
Main responsibilities
• Develop a research plan within the scope of this project for a PhD research program
• Participate in literature searching, data analysis and interpretation 
• Write research articles to be published in peer-reviewed academic journals 
The candidate will work both independently and as part of a team, under supervision of the group leader, and will be encouraged to take an active part in the Centre’s daily activities, depending on needs, interests, and qualifications.

The purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. The research fellow must fulfill the requirements of and take part in the approved PhD program at the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Oslo and is expected to complete the project within the set fellowship period.

The applicant must, in collaboration with her/his supervisor, within three months after employment, work out a complete project description to be attached to the application for admission to the doctoral program. For more information: Doctoral degree: PhD in medicine and health sciences - Faculty of Medicine 
Qualifications
Required skills

• A master’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g., molecular biology, genetics, biostatistics, medicine, psychology, or an equivalent field)
• Strong English and academic writing skills
• Familiarity with programming/scripting languages (e.g., R, Python, and/or Matlab) and big data analysis
• Demonstrated ability to work independently and in a structured manner, and capable of effective collaboration with others 
Preferred skills

• Experience in relevant research, brain and metabolic disorders, multi-omics, and population studies (registry and/or biobank data).
• Experience with machine learning, AI tools and AI-supported codingPersonal skills
• Highly organized, self-driven, and goal-oriented, with strong productivity and attention to detail
• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary research teams
Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal qualifications.

A PhD position is available at the Bruheim research group (https://www.ntnu.edu/employees/per.bruheim) which focuses on Deep Phenotyping of prokaryotic and eukaryotic model systems using Advanced Cultivation Technology and Mass Spectrometry (MS) based Metabolomics, Fluxomics and Lipidomics (https://www.ntnu.edu/ibt/research/micphys#/view/about).

There will be close collaboration with the Otterlei lab and PhD project 1.

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in Systems Engineering - Learning Ecosystem
jobs.description:
PhD Research Fellow in Systems Engineering – Systems Engineering Learning Ecosystem: competencies for systems engineering, AI and business innovation
Do you want to contribute to the development of knowledge, insight and solutions that are relevant to society and working life today and in the future?

We are looking for a PhD research fellow within Systems Engineering.
About the position
Do you want to shape how Norwegian industry learns systems engineering, AI and innovation? Join us as a PhD research fellow at the Department of Science and Industry Systems, campus Kongsberg. Start: May 2027 (at the latest August 2027).

You will be part of SFI CELECT – the Centre for Effective Engineering and Learning in Complex Systems – whose vision is to do more with less, and faster. The centre, funded by the Research Council of Norway, brings together Norway's leading industrial companies and 30 PhD candidates across USN, NTNU and the University of Agder. You will also join the Industrial Research School in Complex Systems (INRESCOS).

The position is a three-year educational position with pure organised research training. A four-year appointment with 25 % career-advancing work may be considered.

You must apply for and be admitted to the doctoral programme in Technology (Systems Engineering) within three months after starting in the position. The programme includes courses of about six months (30 ECTS), an independent thesis, research dissemination, a trial lecture and a public defence.

Your workplace will be campus Kongsberg. You will work closely with several CELECT partner companies through interviews, surveys and workshops.

Campus Kongsberg sits at the heart of one of Norway's strongest technology clusters, with world-leading companies in maritime, defence, aerospace, energy and subsea technology. Research and industry work side by side – giving you a unique network and strong career opportunities in industry or academia.
About the doctoral project
The aim of this PhD is to develop and validate a competency framework for systems engineering, AI and business innovation and translate it into work-integrated learning for Norwegian industry.

Companies lack an overview of which competencies their engineers need and how to build them while they keep working.

In this PhD you will evolve the frameworkin collaboration with industry. Questions you could explore:

• What competency gaps exist in Norwegian industry today?

• Which learning formats actually work for engineers in full-time jobs?

• How can universities and companies co-develop learning that lasts?

You will help shape the final research questions in cooperation with your supervisors and industry partners.

The project is part of SFI CELECT (project PhD5.1), and a workpackage headed by Gerrit Muller. You will run surveys, workshops and pilot courses with CELECT partners such as Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace, TechnipFMC, Siemens Energy, Nammo, Knightec Group, Hive and Herøya Industripark, together with NTNU, UiA and INRESCOS – and your results will feed directly into training at least 200 engineers.

This position is one of several related CELECT PhD positions at USN: it focuses on competence and learning, and complements positions on early design and validation (PhD1.3), life-cycle management of long-living systems (PhD1.4) and early systems integration in systems-of-systems (PhD1.5).

 

Duties

• Complete the doctoral programme up to completion of the doctoral degree within the employment period
• Conduct high-calibre research within the framework described above
• Academic publications in high-quality journals and participate conferences
• Work closely with several partner companies through interviews, surveys and workshops, combining qualitative and quantitative research
• Co-design, pilot and evaluate learning modules and micro-credentials together with CELECT partners
• Report progress and deliver outputs to the CELECT centre
• Participate in the Norwegian Industrial Systems Engineering Research Group (NISE)
• Active involvement in SFI CELECT's doctoral team across NTNU, USN and UiA, including the research school INRESCOS and participation in common workshops, learning events and courses
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign research and educational institutions
• Be prepared for changes in your work tasks after appointment
 
Qualifications
All items are requirements, unless it is specified that they are preferred qualifications.  

• Master's degree (120 ECTS credits) within Systems Engineering, an engineering discipline, industrial economics and technology management, computer science, or a closely related field
• Documented knowledge of relevant methodologies, both quantitative and/or qualitative, at master's level
• Weighted average grade of B or higher on the master's degree and thesis
• The master’s thesis must have been submitted for assessment by the application deadline for the position and approved before starting in the position
• Knowledge of systems engineering and/or business model innovation is preferred
• Knowledge of competency frameworks, engineering education, workplace learning or learning analytics is preferred
• Understanding of AI in engineering is preferred
• Industrial experience from Norwegian industry and or teaching, is preferred
• Proficiency in a Scandinavian language, or Norwegian at level B2, is preferred
• Excellent written and oral English language skills
• Meet the formal requirements for admission to USN's doctoral programmes and the Faculty of Technology, Natural Sciences and Maritime Sciences' doctoral programme in Technology, with the topic of Systems Engineering, no later than three months after starting in the position
 

Personal qualities

In order to be able to complete a doctoral degree, you need to be able to:

• demonstrate motivation and potential for research in the field
• work independently, but also participate in teamwork
•  work in a structured way, set goals, and make plans to achieve them
•  present and discuss your research with other academics
• get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity
• show curiosity and strong motivation for the subject area
• analyse data, assess different perspectives, and draw well-founded conclusions
• work collaboratively in an industrial setting with the CELECT partners
• be flexible and open to adjusting the project plan as necessary
• have the academic skills and personal qualities to be able to complete the doctoral programme within the employment period

PhD Research Fellow in Systems Engineering – AI tools for early validation and development of complex integrated systems
Do you want to contribute to the development of knowledge, insight and solutions that are relevant to society and working life today and in the future?

Some of tomorrow's most innovative systems are shaped by weather, ocean currents and thousands of design choices. How do you know that the design will work before it is built? Help engineers find out with the use of AI. We are looking for a PhD research fellow in Systems Engineering.
About the position
Do you want to help engineers design data-intensive systems where huge amounts of data and a vast design space make early decisions hard? Join us as a PhD research fellow at the Department of Science and Industry Systems, campus Kongsberg. Start: May 2027 (at the latest August 2027).

You will be part of SFI CELECT – the Centre for Effective Engineering and Learning in Complex Systems – whose vision is to do more with less, and faster. The centre, funded by the Research Council of Norway, brings together Norway's leading industrial companies and 30 PhD candidates across USN, NTNU and the University of Agder. You will also join the Industrial Research School in Complex Systems (INRESCOS).

Campus Kongsberg sits at the heart of one of Norway's strongest technology clusters, with world-leading companies in maritime, defence, aerospace, energy and subsea technology. Research and industry work side by side – giving you a unique network and strong career opportunities in industry or academia.

The position is a three-year educational position with pure organised research training. A four-year appointment with 25% career-advancing may be considered.

You must apply for and be admitted to the doctoral programme in Technology (Systems Engineering) within three months of starting. The programme includes courses of about six months (30 ECTS), an independent thesis, research dissemination, a trial lecture and a public defence.

Your main supervisor will be Professor Kristin Falk. Your workplace will be shared between campus Kongsberg and one or several CELECT partner companies: depending on the project, you will spend between 3 and 30 months located at a company's premises. You are expected to be present at campus or at the company during ordinary working hours.
About the doctoral project
The aim of this PhD is to develop AI-supported design methods and tools that enable early validation of complex, data-intensive integrated systems.

Data-intensive systems have huge design spaces, and their behaviour emerges from many interacting factors. Design and operation become intertwined – and today's methods catch problems too late.

In this PhD you will develop AI-supported design assistance: methods and tools, backed by digital twins, that help engineers explore large design spaces and validate systems early. Questions you could explore:

• How are data-intensive systems designed and validated in industry today?

• How can AI and digital twins support early design decisions?

You will help shape the final research questions together with your supervisors and industry partners.

The PhD project is part of SFI CELECT, headed by Professor Kristin Falk. Industrial cases will be selected among CELECT partners such as Kongsberg Maritime, Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace, Siemens Energy, H. Henriksen, Umoe Mandal and cDynamics. Using industry as your laboratory, you will work alongside engineers and systems architects on real development projects.

This position is one of several related CELECT PhD positions at USN: it focuses on early design and validation, and complements positions on life-cycle management of long-living systems (PhD1.4), early systems integration in systems-of-systems (PhD1.5) and competence development for industry (PhD5.1).

You will be part of the Norwegian Industrial Systems Engineering Research Group (NISE).

• Complete the doctoral programme up to completion of the doctoral degree within the employment period
• Conduct high-calibre research within the framework described above
• Academic publications in high-quality journals and conferences
• Actively work with companies in an industry-as-laboratory environment, combining qualitative and quantitative research
• Report progress and deliver outputs to the CELECT centre
• Participate in the Norwegian Industrial Systems Engineering Research Group (NISE)
• Active involvement in SFI CELECT's doctoral team across NTNU, USN and UiA, including the research school INRESCOS, and participation in common workshops, learning events and courses

• Be prepared for changes in your work tasks after appointmentQualifications

• Documented knowledge of relevant methodologies, both quantitative and/or qualitative, at master's level
• Weighted average grade of B or higher on the master's degree and thesis
• The master’s thesis must have been submitted for assessment by the application deadline for the position and approved before starting in the position
• Understanding of and interest in AI/ML and data-driven engineering is preferred
• Knowledge of systems architecting, model-based systems engineering, simulation or digital twins is preferred
• Industrial experience from development of complex or integrated systems (for example maritime, aerospace, manufacture) is preferred
• Proficiency in a Scandinavian language, or Norwegian at level B2, is preferred
• Excellent written and oral English language skills
• Meet the formal requirements for admission to USN's doctoral programmes and the Faculty of Technology, Natural Sciences and Maritime Sciences' doctoral programme in Technology, with the topic of Systems Engineering, no later than three months after starting in the position
 

Personal qualities

In order to be able to complete a doctoral degree, you need to be able to:

• demonstrate motivation and potential for research in the field
• work independently, but also participate in teamwork
•  work in a structured way, set goals, and make plans to achieve them
•  present and discuss your research with other academics
• get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity

• work collaboratively in an industrial setting with the CELECT partners
• be flexible and open to adjusting the project plan as necessary
• have the academic skills and personal qualities to be able to complete the doctoral programme within the employment period

About the project
PhD project 1: New antimicrobial peptides for use as single agents and in combinations builds on data indicating that human plasma represents a reservoir of novel naturally occurring antimicrobial peptides. Some of these peptides display potent antibacterial activity on their own and/or enhance the activity of existing antibiotics. In addition, these antimicrobial peptides may provide a valuable starting point for identifying previously unknown bacterial targets and vulnerabilities. The PhD 1 candidate will participate in identifying and characterizing novel antimicrobial peptides building on previous successful screening efforts. The project will include elucidation of their mechanisms of action and bacterial targets, optimization of promising peptide candidates, and evaluation of their antibacterial activity, alone and in combination with antibiotics, against clinical antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) isolates.

We are looking for a PhD research fellow within Systems Engineering.

Why do companies still end up doing engineering on site during commissioning – even when they have built most of the systems themselves? Find the root causes and change how complex systems come together. 
About the position
Do you want to change how complex systems come together – so that integration happens early, not during commissioning? Join us as a PhD research fellow at the Department of Science and Industry Systems, campus Kongsberg. Start: May 2027 (at the latest August 2027).

You will be part of SFI CELECT – the Centre for Effective Engineering and Learning in Complex Systems – whose vision is to do more with less, and faster. The centre, funded by the Research Council of Norway, brings together Norway's leading industrial companies and 30 PhD candidates across USN, NTNU and the University of Agder. Industrial cases will be selected among CELECT partners such as Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace, Kongsberg Maritime, Forsvarsmateriell, the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI), Nammo, Knightec Group, Fylkeskommuner (Buskerud, Vestfold, Telemark), Kongsberg kommune, Sirkulære Rjukan, and Herøya industry park and others. You will also join the Industrial Research School in Complex Systems (INRESCOS).

The position is a three-year educational position with pure organised research training. A four-year appointment with 25 % career-advancing work may be considered.

You must apply for and be admitted to the doctoral programme in Technology (Systems Engineering) within three months of starting. The programme includes courses of about six months (30 ECTS), an independent thesis, research dissemination, a trial lecture and a public defence.

Your workplace will be shared between campus Kongsberg and one or several CELECT partner companies. Depending on the project, you will spend between 3 and 30 months located at the company's premises. You are expected to be present at campus or at the company during ordinary working hours.

Campus Kongsberg sits at the heart of one of Norway's strongest technology clusters, with world-leading companies in maritime, defence, aerospace, energy and subsea technology. Research and industry work side by side – giving you a unique network and strong career opportunities in industry or academia.
About the doctoral project
The aim of this PhD is to develop a methodology that moves systems integration to an earlier stage of the life cycle, by addressing its organisational, human and technical root causes.

Modern products are part of systems-of-systems that must work together for decades. Integration problems often appear only during commissioning – but their root causes lie much earlier: in how organisations, people and technology interact, and in promises made already in the sales phase.

Questions you could explore:

• What are the root causes of late integration problems?
• How can engineering management be involved early – including in sales – and how do you convince an organisation to do it?
You will help shape the final research questions together with your supervisors and industry partners.

The project is part of SFI CELECT (project PhD1.5), headed by Kristin FalkUsing industry as your laboratory, you will work alongside engineers and systems architects on real development projects. A research stay abroad, for example at TNO-ESI in the Netherlands or DTU in Denmark, may be possible.

The department falls under the Faculty of Humanities of the Norwegian University of Science and Technology NTNU and is located in Trondheim, Norway. We are currently recruiting a PhD Research Fellow in STS who wants to work at the crossroads of infrastructures, security, resilience, and interdisciplinary work across these fields. 

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD research fellow, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a range of leading positions in higher education and research as well as business and administration. 

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department. You will have a daily supervisor at the department, and one or more co-supervisors from across the project team. 
About the project
How do we build a society that is resilient to crises, attacks, and unexpected shocks? A More Resilient Society is a major strategic initiative at NTNU that requires interdisciplinarity and innovative thinking to address complex and socially relevant challenges. A total of 16 PhD candidates will work across faculties and academic communities within the fields of critical societal infrastructure and health preparedness. The aim is to support research that challenges established assumptions and contributes to a safer and more resilient society.  

STRIDE (Synergizing Transport Resilience, Infrastructure, and Defense in Extremes) is one of the projects under the More Resilient Society initiative. STRIDE is a multidisciplinary research project developing a dynamic, multi-risk modeling framework to enhance the resilience of Norway's transport infrastructure against converging climate-driven hazards, such as severe floods and landslides, and geopolitical threats, including targeted sabotage. Moving beyond traditional, brittle "fail-safe" design paradigms, STRIDE operationalizes a "safe-to-fail" approach focused on maintaining critical transport functionality through graceful degradation and rapid recovery across the entire disaster management cycle. As a PhD candidate, you will work within a collaborative, cross-faculty team spanning civil engineering, artificial intelligence, operations research, and science and technology studies.

You will focus on integration of knowledge across academic domains, the operationalization of concepts such as ‘comprehensive resilience’ (Norwegian: totalberedskap) in a multidisciplinary context, and the sociotechnical analysis of infrastructures and their vulnerabilities. 
Duties of the position
You will be offered a position for 4 years as a paid PhD Research Fellow (stipendiat). This will consist of 2,5 years independent research, 0,5 year of courses at PhD level, and 1 year of career-relevant work which may or may not include teaching. More specifically, your duties will be to:

• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out high-quality research within the framework described above
• Produce academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in several research groups at KULT, notably the newly established group on Security Studies (and the related university-wide research group on Security Narratives), and the longstanding Center for Climate, Energy and the Environment (CLEEN).
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Teaching (dependent on the Department’s needs and opportunities)
• Other career-promoting work, such as project support and assistance in grant acquisition.
Changes to your work duties may occur after employment, and flexibility is appreciated.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the Doctoral Programme in Interdisciplinary Studies of Culture (PHKULT, https://www.ntnu.edu/studies/phkult), see also Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a Master's degree in a relevant subject area. Relevant areas include: Science and Technology Studies (STS), fields such as philosophy, history, sociology and anthropology with a distinctly technology-oriented focus, innovation studies and innovation management, and history and philosophy of science (HPS). Within these fields, it is crucial that you demonstrate an affinity with and aptitude for qualitative and interpretive research. We will also consider candidates from the natural and engineering sciences, provided that they can demonstrate affinity and aptitude for humanities and social sciences. 
• Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than August 2027. Documentation needs to be provided with the application, certifying that this is a realistic expectation (e.g. letter from supervisor). 
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Excellent command of the English language, both written and orally.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.

In order to secure a good fit with the project, candidates are strongly recommended to seek informal contact with the envisioned daily supervisor, Govert Valkenburg (see below), in good time before submitting the application, to acquire more detailed information about the project. 
Preferred selection criteria
• Demonstrable interdisciplinary experience, either within the humanities and social sciences (HSS), or even outside HSS, with fields like engineering, natural science or medical science.
• Demonstrable collaborative research experience, including possible internships.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian/Scandinavian. If this is not the case, willingness to learn will be considered an advantage. Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity 
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions 
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work in addition to 1 year of career promotion work. 

The successful candidate will be granted conditional admission to the PHKULT doctoral programme when employed in the PhD research fellow position. It is a prerequisite for continued employment that the requirements for full admission are met within three months, and that you continue to participate in the organized doctoral programme for the remainder of the employment period. For more information about the requirements for full admission, please see Section 6 of the PhD regulations. 

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The application and all required attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no before the deadline. The documents must be in Norwegian, another Scandinavian language or English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. If you are invited for an interview, you must present certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include: 

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees. Include a diploma supplement if your institution offers one, or otherwise a description of the Higher Education system and its grading scales from the country where the degree was obtained.
• CV filled out in Jobbnorge
• Copy of Master's thesis. If the thesis is not in English or a Scandinavian language, add an extended summary in English or Norwegian. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Project outline proposing your approach to the project in terms of research questions, theoretical perspectives and methodological design, as well as a tentativeprogress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages).
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page)
• Any publications or other relevant research work
• Any relevant certificates
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
If all, or parts of, your education has been taken outside Norway, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution does not offer a “diploma supplement”, you must attach information about the grading scale from the education institution. 

We further recommend that you enclose a statement about your education abroad from the Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir). Follow the link to their web site for more information about how to obtain such a statement: Apply for recognition of foreign higher education. See also NTNU’s web site for documentation requirements for education obtained outside Norway. 

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact research professor Govert Valkenburg, govert.valkenburg@ntnu.no. If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact Elisabeth Leite, email: elisabeth.leite@ntnu.no.

Want to build and ship AI systems that professionals rely on for real work? Crunched is looking for a senior engineer who wants to own the hard problems from architecture to production – in a small team moving fast.

Crunched builds an autonomous AI analyst for strategy, finance and advisory workflows, bringing AI agents into Excel rather than asking users to change how they work. The company is backed by Y Combinator and has raised NOK 55 million in seed funding.

The engineering challenge goes beyond a chatbot: agents, data flows and reliable execution need to work together in a product used for consequential decisions. You will work close to the founders, customers and engineers, with room to shape the stack and engineering culture. This is a high-intensity, on-site role in Oslo – a fit for someone who values ownership and building together in person.

• Build and ship autonomous AI workflows used by professional customers
• Work across Python, TypeScript, React, Postgres, FastAPI and LangGraph
• Own features from architecture and implementation to production operation

• Strong professional experience building and shipping software

• Experience shipping production systems with high ownership

• Comfortable working five days on-site in OsloWhat we offer

• Direct customer impact and short decision paths
